clue.text: Rifle fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to plunder a captured town
second meaning: to dismiss someone from a job

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gun being discharged, but 'Rifle' is a verb meaning to ransack and 'fire' means to dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, and to sack an employee is to dismiss them from work.

clue.text: A drop in the ocean?

parts.note: surface reading: the idiom for a tiny, insignificant amount
setter's reading: a literal descent into the sea, as by a returning space capsule

explanation.walkthrough: The familiar idiom for something negligible is read literally: a spacecraft dropping into the sea at the end of a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A space capsule's landing in the sea is the event that ends many missions, a literal fall into the water.

clue.text: Tending to comply with social norms, scorn motif that's out of order

definitions.text: Tending to comply with social norms

indicators.note: letters that are out of order have lost their proper sequence and must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who follows convention looks down on a design element that breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A conformist is a person who goes along with accepted behaviour, so the word works as an adjective for compliance with norms.

clue.text: Argument applied to merit of poet

parts.note: to have words is to argue
worth is value or merit

explanation.surface: A literary critic's dispute about how good a poet really is.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet of the Lake District.

clue.text: Come clean about cricket side seizing wicket and winning

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab it and hold it within one's grasp

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
W is the scorecard abbreviation for a wicket
a team that is ahead is said to be up

explanation.surface: A cricket team admits to something after taking a wicket and pulling ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, the same idiom as coming clean about a wrongdoing.

clue.text: Pancake — declines cold one

parts.note: something that declines drops
C for cold, as on a tap
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a café turns down a pancake that has gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop scone is a small thick Scottish pancake cooked on a griddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small thick pancake made by dropping batter onto a hot griddle.

clue.text: A light sauce may create a superficial impression

parts.note: a window is a light in a building
a salad dressing is a sauce

explanation.surface: A cook observes that a thin sauce can make a dish look better than it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Window dressing is a display meant to make something look more favourable than it really is.

clue.text: Cairo beautician's dress

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A beauty salon owner in Egypt shows off an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no indicator word: the possessive simply sets the two words side by side for the answer to span them.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment, a kind of dress.

clue.text: Cannabis in dish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang short form of hashish
second meaning: a meal of chopped meat and potato fried together

explanation.surface: A drug has been slipped into someone's food.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is slang for the resin of cannabis and also a fried dish of chopped leftovers.

clue.text: US dance director following tradition in Mayfair

definitions.note: the definition names where the answer is, not what it is

parts.note: Busby Berkeley directed the lavish dance numbers of Hollywood musicals
square means conventional, sticking to tradition

explanation.surface: An American choreographer keeps to tradition while working in a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an upmarket district of central London; 'tradition' must stand for the adjective sense of square, old-fashioned and conventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkeley Square is a garden square in Mayfair, famous from the song about a nightingale singing there.

clue.text: Light later around northern Norway

indicators.note: around means wrapping one word about another so that it sits inside

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Daylight lingers longer in the far north of Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable light in a protective case.

clue.text: Several books in one PSV

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single volume collecting several works
second meaning: a public service vehicle, an old name for a bus

explanation.walkthrough: PSV is the British licensing term for a public service vehicle such as a bus or coach.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is both a collected edition of several books and the full original name of the bus.

clue.text: Drop of sweet white wine in jar

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the initial of this word
hock is a white wine from the German Rhineland

explanation.surface: A little dessert wine stored in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a pot to keep wine in; it is the verb, to jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a sudden jolt, which is what a shock is.

clue.text: Sauce — favourite covering piece of savoury duck

indicators.note: covering means lying over and around something so it is enclosed

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: a piece is only a small part, here just the first letter

parts.note: the initial of this word
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A favourite sauce spread over a portion of savoury duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and cheese.

clue.text: Young boy providing shelter for English commando

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside one's own cover

parts.note: a boy's name
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A lad takes in an English soldier from an elite unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young boy' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Young' is one piece and 'boy' another.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green Beret is a member of the Royal Marines commandos or US Special Forces, named for their headgear.

clue.text: Machine, pretty faulty having loose wire inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within another group of letters
something faulty is broken, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged as the outer part

indicators.note: loose letters are free to move about and settle in a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged as the inner part

explanation.surface: An electrical gadget is broken because a wire inside has come loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A typewriter is a mechanical machine for printing letters onto paper.

clue.text: Comprehensive defeat ahead of classic motor race

parts.note: a demolition is a crushing defeat
the Derby is one of the five English Classic horse races

explanation.surface: A team is thrashed just before a famous race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Classics are five historic English flat horse races, of which the Derby at Epsom is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: A demolition derby is a contest in which old cars crash into each other until one is left running.

clue.text: Unnecessary repetition got layout looking higgledy-piggledy

indicators.note: higgledy-piggledy means jumbled in confusion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor complains that a page design looks a mess and says the same thing twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautology is saying the same thing twice in different words, a needless repetition.

clue.text: Message on a pc — 'Why rewire house, dilapidated end of terrace?'

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so its letters are reassembled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A puzzled owner asks why anyone would rewire a run-down terraced house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pc' looks like a personal computer, but it is a postcard. A terrace is a row of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wish you were here is the stock phrase written on a holiday postcard.

clue.text: Ring from Ecuador's capital on moving round to the centre

indicators.note: to the centre says where the taken letter is put back, in the middle
moving a letter means taking it out of its present place

parts.note: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador
the letter is round in shape

explanation.surface: A ring brought back from the Ecuadorian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecuador's capital' tempts a single letter E; here it is the whole city name, whose final round letter shifts into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoit is a ring tossed at a peg in the game of quoits.

clue.text: Volunteers to entertain a politician here in Florida

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Volunteer reservists host a visiting politician in the Sunshine State.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida, so 'here' points to a place.

clue.text: Serious honour received by senior

indicators.note: something received by a person is taken in and held by them

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviation for senior
Officer of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: An elderly person is solemnly awarded an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober means grave and solemn as well as not drunk.

clue.text: Fish when in outskirts of Bowness

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
outskirts are the edges of a place, so the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of this town name
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: An angler names a fish found near a Lake District town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowness-on-Windermere is a town on England's largest lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass is a common sea and freshwater fish.

clue.text: Old garment, article obtained on the way over

indicators.note: going over turns things the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the indefinite article
obtained means got

explanation.surface: An item of ancient clothing picked up while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment of citizens in ancient Rome.

clue.text: A mostly outspoken party demanding fruit

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
vocal means outspoken
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A rather loud guest at a party insists on having fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped green fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Remain uneasy heading for Tokyo Tower

indicators.note: uneasy suggests unsettled, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the initial of this word

explanation.surface: A traveller stays nervous before setting off for Tokyo Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tokyo Tower' reads as the landmark; only 'Tower' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Cry as cadet condemned a coward

indicators.note: something condemned is ruined and ready to be broken up and remade

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainee officer is mocked as a coward for crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaredy-cat is a childish taunt for a timid, fearful person.

clue.text: Can cause trouble

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to ... things up, provoking a row

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as the verb 'be able to'; it is the noun, slang for prison, as is stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for jail, and to stir is to make mischief by provoking discord.
